localContext: Port Morris, known for its industrial character along the Harlem River waterfront and proximity to major thoroughfares like the Bruckner Expressway, presents unique stinging-insect challenges with its mix of older warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and emerging residential developments. The neighborhood's older structures — loading docks, building eaves, soffits, and wall voids — provide ideal nesting sites for wasp, hornet, and yellow jacket colonies throughout the warmer months. Carpenter bees bore into wooden loading-bay frames and fascia boards. Ground-nesting yellow jackets colonize gaps in pavement and unmaintained soil near the waterfront.
